content: Cefmetazole is classified as a cephamycin antibiotic and is typically grouped with second-generation cephalosporins. The chemical structure of cefmetazole includes an N-methylthiotetrazole (NMTT or 1-MTT) side chain, which is also present in several other cephalosporins. During the metabolic breakdown of cefmetazole in the body, free NMTT is released. This compound has been associated with hypoprothrombinemia, likely due to its inhibition of the enzyme vitamin K epoxide reductase. Additionally, NMTT can cause a disulfiram-like reaction when ethanol is consumed, as it inhibits the enzyme aldehyde dehydrogenase. Cefmetazole exhibits broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity and has demonstrated efficacy in treating infections caused by bacteria responsible for urinary tract infections and skin infections. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) data for cefmetazole has been established for several clinically significant microorganisms.
